newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Sky City on track for NZ$35.8 mln yr net.
newsitem.headline: Sky City on track for NZ$35.8 mln yr net.

text.p: Casino operator Sky City on Monday said it was on track to achieve a forecast profit of NZ$35.8 million for the full 1996/97 year.
Earlier, Sky City reported net earnings for the first half to December 31 of $18.2 million and declared a first half dividend of 13 NZ cents per share.
It said the first-half profit reflected its expectation that the listing profile projection of NZ$35.8 million for the 1997 year would be an appropriate target.

"The company is on track to achieve that result, however much will depend on the market's reaction and acceptance of the Harrah's Club gaming facility which was opened on February 14," the company said.
Sky said the level of daily gaming machine revenue compared favourably with Australian casinos.
Average table win per day had fallen from $3,200 in the five months to June 30 to $2,800 in the six months to December 31, but was still significantly ahead of the profile projection of $2,340.
"Whilst table revenue has remained relatively constant over this period, the reduced average win is in part simply a consequence of increased levels of player experience," Sky said.
The Sky City hotel opened at the end of May and operated successfully during the period, experiencing a rapid increase in occupancy.

"Budgeted occupancy for the period of 75 percent, already high for a large hotel in its first year of operation, has been exceeded, and we are now able to focus on increasing average achieved room rate. Overall the hotel revenue position is very pleasing," the company said.

Development of some other business operations had taken longer than expected. Cafe Fortuna, the main restaurant serving gaming customers, attracted good support, but the other restaurants had not yet achieved expected patronage levels.
Restructuring of the food operation was currently under way, with product offerings being adjusted to improve profitability.
"As part of this process, the cost structure of the business is being matched to the scale of the business being achieved," Sky City said.
It said its Sky Tower, which includes a viewing platform and telecommunications facilities, was almost completed for an opening in July.

The company said it was currently considering development optinos for the site adjoining the Sky City complex, and said it was well advanced in preparations to lodge an application for a casino licence in Queenstown in the South Island.
